newsitem.title: CHINA: China bans Taiwan hog imports over disease fears.
newsitem.headline: China bans Taiwan hog imports over disease fears.

text.p: China has banned imports from Taiwan of hogs, oxen, sheep and other cloven-hooved animals to prevent an epidemic of foot-and-mouth disease from spreading to the mainland, agricultural officials said on Wednesday.

More than one million Taiwanese hogs have been killed in an army-led eradication campaign to curb the spread of the highly contagious disease, which has erupted in more than 1,000 hog farms in Taiwan since March 19.

State media reported that China was confident it could help Taiwan through the crisis, but an official of the Ministry of Agriculture said Beijing had banned all imports of potentially vulnerable animals from March 27.
"The ban is aimed at preventing infection in the mainland from Taiwanese imports," he said.
Figures were unavailable for the value of imports from Taiwan of cloven-hooved animals, he said.

The official China Daily newspaper said there was little direct or indirect hog trade between the mainland and Taiwan, Beijing's arch-rival since defeated Nationalist armies fled there at the end of the Chinese civil war in 1949.
Taiwan has already banned all pork exports to prevent the foot-and-mouth outbreak from spreading.

Chinese officials and experts were confident they could help Taipei to weather the financially disastrous epidemic, the China Daily quoted Chen Zhongyi of the Ministry of Agriculture's Taiwan Affairs Office as saying.
"If Taiwan agrees, the mainland will be able to help," Chen said.
China had yet to receive a reply to a message of sympathy and an offer of help sent by officials to Taipei, the China Daily said.
Taiwan officials have said quality problems and political obstacles mean a deal to accept mainland vaccines for the island's high-risk hogs is unlikely.
Mainland experts believed it was wrong for Taiwan to import European and U.S. vaccines, which were less effective against foot-and-mouth disease in hogs, said the China Daily.
The agricultural ministry would over the next two or three years prepare a list of vaccine suppliers on the mainland who could provide safe and effective vaccines, it said.
"Only after that length of time can the disease be brought under control," it said.
